task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of September 8, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style reported feature about the Aster Fold costume bank and how shared garments change the cost and practical work of school theater.

facts.text: A June 2026 costume-room note records coordinator Omi Savren pinning a temporary hem while a drama teacher compared the garment with a production's color plan.
Aster Fold serves 14 member schools from a rented room in an arts center.
Each school pays $180 annually, generating $2,520 in annual membership receipts if all current memberships are paid.
The service recorded 1,200 garment checkouts last year, including repeated loans of the same clothing.
The checkout count is not an inventory of 1,200 distinct costumes or a count of student performers.
The current terms charge a separate $2 cleaning contribution per returned garment; the packet gives no annual return count or total cleaning receipts.
Membership permits requests subject to availability; it does not guarantee a full matching cast wardrobe for every production.
Schools may make reversible alterations but must seek approval before cutting or permanently changing garments.
Popular sizes and neutral coats are booked earlier than unusual costume pieces, according to the reservation ledger.
Drama teacher Nera Vossel shifted one production's color choices after the requested coats were already reserved by another school.
Vossel said, "Borrowing changes the budget, but it also asks the production to work with what is actually on the rail."
Savren is paid for eight hours a week; volunteers help sort returns and perform simple repairs.
Membership and cleaning receipts are supplemented by arts-center support and donations; they do not cover all staffing and room costs alone.
Some donated garments require more alteration or cleaning than their likely future use justifies, and the bank does not accept every donation.
Savren said, "A free coat can still arrive with an expensive amount of work inside it."
The bank has not measured a uniform per-school saving because schools would otherwise buy, hire, make or reuse different items.
Late returns can affect the next school's fitting period even when an item comes back undamaged.
The bank's loan records use garment identifiers and school contacts, not pupils' personal measurements.
The collection began with costumes from a dissolved amateur theater company in 2019.
A proposal for more paid coordinator hours remains unfunded, and the current service cannot promise to add more member schools.

forbidden_additions: Guaranteed complete wardrobes, 1,200 distinct costumes or a uniform school saving
All donations are costless or extra coordinator hours have been financed
